title: Effect-binding lookup is O(total project events) per call
description:
RAISED BY worker-247da23f while fixing task-d92b1b15a5b048e49671ed34990fa4a1 (defect 2). Filed rather than solved, per that task's rail 4: "If the correct fix is an index or a per-aggregate query instead of a global scan, raise that as a design decision rather than landing it unannounced."

WHAT LANDED, AND WHAT DID NOT. task-d92b1b15 removed `MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64` from `scanForEffect` in apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts. That constant imposed a hard ceiling of 64 x 100 = 6,400 TOTAL PROJECT EVENTS, past which `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` refused FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE permanently, for every effect. That correctness bug is fixed and is now pinned by two tests at a literal 6,500-event store in foundation-launch-authority.test.ts.

THE REMAINING PROBLEM IS PERFORMANCE, NOT CORRECTNESS. `scanForEffect` still reads the GLOBAL event stream from cursor 0n via `store.readEventsAfter(cursor, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE)`, and it CANNOT exit early on a hit: its only success exit is `if (!read.hasMore)`, because the answer it owes is not "an activation matched" but "EXACTLY ONE did". It must therefore exhaust the entire stream on every call, decoding every event whose type is EffectActivationCommitted along the way. So each effect-binding lookup is O(total project events), and that cost grows monotonically for the life of the project.

WHY IT IS A DESIGN DECISION AND NOT A PATCH. The scan exists because `CoordinationEffectQuery` carries an effectId but NOT the idempotency key that the activation aggregate id derives from (`deriveActivationAggregateId(effectIntent.aggregateId, effectIntent.idempotencyKey)`). Given the key, the lookup would be a single `readEvents(aggregateId)`. So the candidate answers are:
  (a) carry the idempotency key (or the derived aggregate id) on the query - a schema change, which was explicitly out of scope for task-d92b1b15;
  (b) a durable per-effect index mapping intentId -> aggregate id, maintained in the same transaction as the activation commit - note task-d92b1b15's rail 1 forbade this ledger from owning a side table, so ownership needs deciding;
  (c) a per-aggregate or indexed query on the store surface, so uniqueness can be proven without a full walk.
Each has a different owner and a different blast radius, which is why this is a task rather than a follow-up commit.

CONSTRAINT THAT ANY ANSWER MUST PRESERVE: the uniqueness proof. Whatever replaces the walk must still detect a SECOND matching activation on a different aggregate and refuse FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS. The test "still refuses a SECOND matching activation found past the old 6,400 ceiling" (foundation-launch-authority.test.ts) exists precisely to stop scale being bought with that invariant, and must stay green.

NOT URGENT: the scan is correct at every size now, and the cost is a full sequential page walk of a local SQLite table. This is filed so the cliff is owned rather than rediscovered.
definitionOfDone: A decision is recorded naming which of (a) carry the idempotency key on CoordinationEffectQuery, (b) a durable per-effect index, or (c) an indexed store query is taken, and which component owns the chosen surface.

The chosen surface answers readCurrentEffectSessionBinding without walking the whole global stream, proven by a test that drives the store past the existing literal 6,500-event mark and asserts the lookup does not read every event.

The uniqueness proof survives: a second matching activation on a different aggregate is still detected and still refuses FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS with its exact code and layer. The existing test 'still refuses a SECOND matching activation found past the old 6,400 ceiling' stays green and unmodified.
No page-count ceiling is reintroduced. Any bound on the work done must be a bound the store enforces, not a constant that turns a large project into a permanent SCAN_INCOMPLETE refusal.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0 with each leg's exit code read separately.
taskRails: Do not reintroduce a page-count cap on scanForEffect. A cap is not a termination guarantee - the empty-page-with-hasMore and cursor-must-advance guards already own termination - and a cap fails closed into a refusal indistinguishable from a real authority answer.

The uniqueness proof is the invariant, not the walk. Any faster lookup must still refuse FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS on a second matching activation. Buying speed by returning on first match is a wrong answer.

If the answer needs a side table, decide its OWNER first. task-d92b1b15's rail 1 forbade the activation ledger from writing daemon-owned tables inside its commit transaction, so an index maintained transactionally with the activation commit needs that constraint revisited explicitly rather than quietly.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND UNDERSTAND THE PROOF YOU ARE ABOUT TO REPLACE — this step is the whole risk of the task. Measure at current HEAD first (measured at abc3dcf).
THE LANDED SURFACE, all three legs of the facade, so you do not re-derive task-69's work: `readEventsByTypeAfter` exists at `packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts:354`, at `event-read-model.ts:98`, AND — the facade lesson from msg-de56010e — as a `DecisionLedgerCore` delegate at `decision-ledger.ts:77` (declaration) and `:148-153` (delegation). All three are committed. The daemon side is what is missing.
THE HOT PATH: `scanForEffect` in `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts` (375 lines). It walks EVERY global position from 1 to the captured horizon in pages of `SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 100` (:107), discarding everything whose `eventType !== ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE` (:288). That discard is the O(total project events) cost the title names.
THE PROOF YOU MUST REPLACE, AND THE HONEST TRADE. Today's completeness proof is POSITIONAL CONTIGUITY, and the code says so: "Contiguity IS the completeness proof: a skipped position is an event this scan never judged" (:284-285). It is self-verifying — the reader proves it saw everything WITHOUT trusting the store's `hasMore`. Four checks enforce it: per-event `globalPosition !== position || position > horizon`; `position === cursor` (no progress); `read.nextCursor !== position`; and `read.hasMore !== (position < horizon)`.
A TYPE-FILTERED READ DESTROYS CONTIGUITY — matches are sparse by construction, so three of those four checks stop meaning what they meant. The replacement proof MUST rest on the filtered pager's own `hasMore`/`nextCursor` contract, which is strictly weaker: it TRUSTS the store where the old walk verified it. That is a real reduction in self-verification and you must state it in the module comment rather than quietly swapping one loop for another. What keeps it sound: task-69 pinned the exact behaviour this depends on — at the last match, the filtered page reports `hasMore:false`/`nextCursor:<last match>` even when unfiltered rows still follow. Read that contract test in `packages/store/src/event-read-model-contract.test.ts` before relying on it.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and every failing file as your before-set. Both are expected RED from foreign slices; repair none of it.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — pin EQUIVALENCE before pinning speed, because a faster scan that answers differently is a regression, not an optimisation. Add to `activation-ledger-reader.test.ts`:
(a) EQUIVALENCE ACROSS THE OUTCOME SET. For each outcome the current scan can produce — a unique binding found, no binding found, `FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS` (two aggregates claiming one effect id), `FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE`, `FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED`, `FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE` — assert the exact code AND that it is unchanged by the rewrite. These are the semantics the prior handoff warned must not move.
(b) THE NO-EARLY-RETURN RULE. `:295-296` says the walk runs to the horizon even after a hit, "because the answer is not 'one matched' but 'exactly one did'". Write a case where the FIRST match is followed by a SECOND, later, different-aggregate match: the answer must be AMBIGUOUS. A filtered rewrite that returns on first hit passes every other test and fails only this one.
(c) SPARSE POSITIONS. Seed a ledger where activation events sit at non-adjacent global positions with unrelated events between them — this is the shape that breaks positional contiguity and the shape the filtered pager must handle. Assert the scan still answers correctly.
(d) HORIZON BOUNDING SURVIVES. An activation event committed PAST the captured horizon must not affect the answer: "growth past H is not this answer's business" (:262-263). Assert a match beyond H is neither returned nor treated as ambiguity.
(e) COST. Assert the scan reads a number of events proportional to MATCHES, not to total events — count store reads through a counting port wrapper and assert an explicit literal bound that today's implementation would FAIL. Without a failing-today assertion this task has no proof it changed anything.

implementationPlan.description:
REPLACE THE SCAN, AND WRITE DOWN THE NEW COMPLETENESS PROOF. Rewrite `scanForEffect` to walk `readEventsByTypeAfter(ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE, cursor, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE)` instead of `readEventsAfter`, dropping the per-event type discard at :288 since the store now filters.
THE REPLACEMENT PROOF, which must be stated in the module comment where the contiguity paragraph is today — do not leave a comment describing a proof the code no longer performs:
- Every returned item's `globalPosition` is STRICTLY INCREASING and `<= horizon`; a repeat or a decrease is `FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE`. Strict increase replaces contiguity as the ordering guarantee.
- Every returned item's `eventType` IS the activation type. Assert it even though the store filters: it costs one comparison and it is what keeps the guard honest if the filter ever regresses.
- `read.nextCursor` must ADVANCE past the previous cursor whenever items were returned; a non-advancing cursor is INCOMPLETE. Note this differs from today's `nextCursor !== position` check, because under the filtered pager `nextCursor` is the LAST MATCH's position, not `cursor + items.length`.
- Terminate on `hasMore === false`. Task-69 pinned that the filtered page reports `hasMore:false` at the last match even when unfiltered rows still follow — that is the contract this loop rests on, and the module comment must say so by name so a future reader can find the test that guarantees it.
- Keep the horizon bound: a match past H refuses nothing and is simply outside this answer.
PRESERVE EXACTLY, because they are the semantics, not the mechanism: no early return on a hit (run to completion, since the question is "exactly one"); the ambiguity refusal when two distinct aggregates claim one effect id; and every existing `UnknownCode` mapping.
LINE BUDGET: the file is at 375 of 400. Removing the discard and the contiguity arithmetic should roughly pay for the new comment, but MEASURE with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). If it crosses 400, split `scanForEffect` into a sibling module with its own one-line `.js` bridge rather than compressing the comment away — the comment is the deliverable here as much as the loop.
implementationPlan.note:
SCAN REPLACED AND THE NEW COMPLETENESS PROOF WRITTEN DOWN. Both owned suites GREEN: `pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.test.ts src/activation/foundation-launch-authority.test.ts` EXIT=0, count lines "Test Files 2 passed (2)" / "Tests 60 passed (60)". The four cases red at step 2 are the four that flipped.

THE LOOP. `store.readEventsByTypeAfter(ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE, cursor, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE)`; the per-event type discard is gone. The `remaining`-clamped page limit is gone with it and `SCAN_PAGE_LIMIT` is deleted: `remaining` counted GLOBAL positions, which is not a bound on MATCHES and would have clamped the page to a number with no meaning under a filter.

THE COMMENT REPLACES THE CONTIGUITY PARAGRAPH IN ITS OWN SLOT - the retired text is not left standing anywhere. It states the trade in the plainest words I could write: "THE COMPLETENESS PROOF CHANGED, AND IT GOT WEAKER. THIS IS THE HONEST TRADE." It says the retired walk derived each expected position as cursor+1 and so proved it judged every event WITHOUT trusting the store; that a type filter makes matches sparse by construction so contiguity is false on every healthy ledger; and that completeness now RESTS ON THE PAGER'S CONTRACT, trusting `hasMore` where the old walk verified positions itself. It names the pin BY FILE AND CASE - `packages/store/src/event-read-model-contract.test.ts`, "pages only exact event-type matches across an interleaved ledger" - so a reader can find the test that guarantees `hasMore:false`/`nextCursor:<last match>` at the final match while unfiltered rows still follow. It also records what this cost before: O(total project events), growing for the life of the project.

THE FOUR REPLACEMENT GUARDS, each named in the comment and each with a hostile case:
1. STRICT INCREASE replaces contiguity: `if (event.globalPosition <= position) return no(SCAN_INCOMPLETE)` then `position = event.globalPosition`. Catches a repeat and a decrease.
2. FILTER HONESTY: the event type is re-compared even though the store filters - one comparison, and the guard that stays honest if the filter regresses to the unfiltered stream.
3. CURSOR NAMES THE LAST RETURNED POSITION: `read.nextCursor !== position` where `position` is now the LAST ITEM'S globalPosition, not cursor + items.length. Same expression as before, different meaning, and the comment says so.
4. AN EMPTY PAGE MAY NOT CLAIM MORE: `position === cursor` means no item advanced anything, so `hasMore` there is the never-ending walk and is refused; without `hasMore` it is the ordinary empty tail and terminates.
Termination: `if (!read.hasMore) break` after the cursor check, and `cursor = position` only on a strictly greater position, so progress is guaranteed and the horizon still bounds the walk. NO page-count cap was reintroduced (task rail 1).

HORIZON. `if (position > horizon) { beyondHorizon = true; break; }` skips the item and ends the walk. A match past H is not returned, does NOT count toward ambiguity, and refuses nothing - both halves are asserted by "ignores an activation committed past the captured horizon".

DELIBERATE SEMANTIC CHANGE, and it is the one the plan authorised: at the horizon, `hasMore === true` is no longer a refusal. The retired `read.hasMore !== (position < horizon)` check refused SCAN_INCOMPLETE there. Under a filtered pager `hasMore` is computed over MATCHES, so a true `hasMore` at H is ordinary concurrent growth. Refusing on it would rebuild, at the horizon, exactly the permanent-refusal cliff this task removes at the page cap. "bounds a continuously advancing scan to the captured horizon" pins the new answer (ABSENT/NOT_FOUND, pageReads 3 against horizon 3) and its comment records the change.

Today's completeness proof is POSITIONAL CONTIGUITY and the code states it at :284-285: “Contiguity IS the completeness proof: a skipped position is an event this scan never judged.” It is SELF-VERIFYING — the reader proves it saw everything without trusting the store's `hasMore`. A TYPE-FILTERED READ DESTROYS CONTIGUITY by construction — matches are sparse — so three of those four checks stop meaning what they meant, and `nextCursor` changes meaning (it becomes the LAST MATCH's position, not `cursor + items.length`).
